decisions.reason: This cutting and creasing finisher is close to the core portfolio and has its own page, so keeping it as a traded product costs little while demand is still uncertain, which makes the option worth holding.

UV spot varnishing is distant from the core and its prospects are the most uncertain, but the German premiere drew early attention and as a distributed Duplo product it is cheap to keep, so the option stays open until results show more.
The sheet preparation module builds on existing systems and adds modular value at low holding cost, so there is no evidence yet to justify abandoning it.
The B2 multifinisher was featured as a flagship on the home page and fits the move toward automated finishing, so its value is still unfolding and further commitment is warranted.
The hybrid saddle stitcher is close to the core booklet-making business, and keeping it on its own page is inexpensive while market response is still uncertain.
The folding add-on already shows a customer installation with inline integration, an early positive signal at low holding cost that supports keeping it.
